requirements.evidence: Full contract is there: migrations with cascades, unique (entity_id, slug)/(queue_id, code) and the recommended index (database/migrations/2026_10_29_044443_create_tickets_table.php:12-23); enums; InactiveQueueException; Queue/Ticket models with the contracted casts and relations; Entity::queues(); IssueTicket with negative-priority check, locked fresh re-read of the queue, retry on unique collisions (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:29-69); write-once saving guard (app/Models/Ticket.php:48-63); nextCode by insertion order that skips malformed codes and grows past 999 (app/Models/Ticket.php:89-104); factories with forQueue and explicit-code handling. Gaps: nextCode takes the last surviving row, so deleting the most recent ticket (A001..A003, delete A003) gives A003 again, against 'deleting a ticket does not reuse its number'. Ticket::call checks the in-memory status without re-reading or locking the row (app/Models/Ticket.php:124), so a stale instance can call an already-called ticket a second time.

conventions.evidence: Domain write goes through App\Actions\IssueTicket; migrations have reversible down() and generator-style timestamps; $fillable is set; business-rules.md, database-schema.md and CHANGELOG [Unreleased] are updated; public methods have PHPDoc. Deviations: authorization in Ticket::call is a hand-rolled EntityMembership query (app/Models/Ticket.php:117-122) instead of a policy/gate. The two new models declare fillable differently: #[Fillable] attribute in Queue (app/Models/Queue.php:12) vs protected $fillable in Ticket (app/Models/Ticket.php:17).

security.evidence: No HTTP/Livewire surface. Call is restricted to entity members and the ticket is left unchanged on denial (tested at tests/Feature/Queue/IssueTicketTest.php:256-269). Issuance re-reads is_active under lockForUpdate. Limited gaps: the membership check bypasses the policy layer, and Ticket $fillable includes status/called_at/called_by_user_id (app/Models/Ticket.php:17-26), which will allow mass-assignment of call fields once inputs reach the model. The call race noted under requirements can double-record a call.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/Queue/IssueTicketTest.php covers schema/uniques, both cascades, enums, factories (A001/A002, explicit 'A-X'), every nextCode example from the task, issuance defaults, stale inactive queue with nothing persisted, a real collision-retry test, negative priority, write-once, single call, non-waiting call and non-member call. Missing: no test for deleting the last ticket (the reuse case), concurrent or stale double call, the labels_i18n cast, or the calledBy()/tickets() relations. One duplicated assertion (line 82 vs 85).

simplicity.evidence: Mostly direct. nextCode loads every code of the queue (->pluck('code') at app/Models/Ticket.php:94) on each issuance, so the cost grows with queue size. The QueryException fallback with SQLSTATE '23000' or a substring match on 'unique' (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:59-80) is speculative because UniqueConstraintViolationException is already caught, and '23000' also matches FK violations. QueueFactory::inactive() (database/factories/QueueFactory.php:30) is never used.

readability.evidence: Clear names, short methods and helpful comments (e.g. the stale-instance comment at app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:38-39). Small issues: the fillable style differs between Queue and Ticket, the RuntimeException after the retry loop is unreachable, and there is a duplicated assertion in the queue factory test.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: models, enums, exception, action, factories, migrations, docs, changelog and tests. Out-of-scope items (call-next selection, UI, totem API) are not touched; the only extra is the small unused QueueFactory::inactive() state.

issues.explanation: call() checks the possibly stale in-memory status without re-reading or locking the row, or using a conditional update, so two instances of the same ticket can both call it, breaking 'called exactly once'.

nextCode uses the last surviving row, so deleting the most recent ticket (A001..A003, delete A003) gives A003 again; this contradicts 'deleting a ticket does not reuse its number' and the docs' claim that deleted tickets do not free numbers.
Authorization is a hand-rolled EntityMembership query inside the model rather than a policy/gate, as the conventions require.
Every issuance loads all codes of the queue into memory to find the last valid one, so the cost grows with queue size.
The extra QueryException branch is speculative: UniqueConstraintViolationException is already caught, SQLSTATE 23000 also matches FK violations, and the substring match on 'unique' is brittle.
Queue uses the #[Fillable] attribute while Ticket uses protected $fillable; the two new sibling models are inconsistent.
$fillable includes status, called_at and called_by_user_id, so the call fields can be mass-assigned and bypass call()'s checks once inputs reach the model.
The entity instance assertion is duplicated, and there are no tests for the labels_i18n cast, the calledBy()/tickets() relations, or the deleted-last-ticket case.
The inactive() factory state is added but never used.

review.summary: The change adds the queues/tickets persistence, enums, models, factories and the IssueTicket action, which re-reads the queue under a lock and retries code collisions. It comes with thorough tests and docs and changelog updates. It meets nearly the whole contract; the remaining issues are minor: call() trusts the in-memory status, a deleted last ticket's number gets reused, the membership check bypasses policies, and nextCode loads every code of the queue. Approvable with small follow-ups.
